study.title: Gender differences in brain activity underlying acupuncture sensations at LR3: a task-based fMRI study
study.study_design: task-based fMRI study with block-design acupuncture task, within-session task vs. baseline comparison, stratified by gender
study.population: healthy volunteers aged 20-35, right-handed, recruited from the First Affiliated Hospital of Anhui University of Traditional Chinese Medicine
study.inclusion_criteria: 1. age: 20-35 years old; 2. right-handed; 3. no acupuncture 1 month before the experiment; 4. Patients had not taken any medications for 30 days prior to enrollment and during the trial period.; 5. no history of alcohol, drug dependence, or head surgery; 6. no contraindications to MRI scanning; 7. able to tolerate the noise generated by the MRI machine during testing; 8. no claustrophobia; 9. women were not menstruating; 10 signed the informed consent before experimentation
study.exclusion_criteria: 1. poor compliance, which affected data collection according to the operation instructions; 2. Excessive head movement (head movement >3° or 3 mm); 3. abnormal body movement occurring during the scanning process; 4. subjects withdrew voluntarily due to personal reasons

arms.dropouts: 4 females excluded due to excessive head movement
3 males excluded due to excessive head movement, 2 males excluded due to partial image loss

interventions.session_duration_exact: total scan time for each run was 380 s

neuroimaging_methods.preprocessing_software_exact: SPM12 based on MATLAB 2017b (Mathworks Inc., USA)
neuroimaging_methods.coordinate_space_reported_exact: MNI (inferred from AAL atlas use; not explicitly stated in methods text)
neuroimaging_methods.smoothing_exact: Gaussian kernel (full width at maximum = 6 mm)
neuroimaging_methods.motion_exclusion_exact: Remove data from subjects with translation >3 mm or rotation >3°
neuroimaging_methods.filtering_exact: bandpass filter with a bandwidth of 0.2–0.008 Hz
neuroimaging_methods.global_signal_regression_exact: linear regression to remove irrelevant noise time series including head motion-related Friston-24, cerebrospinal fluid, and white matter signals, as well as their time-differenced signals (derivatives) and task-related signals

statistical_thresholds_exact: Activation: voxel level p < 0.001, cluster level p < 0.05 (FWE correction)

extraction_notes.note: The paper's Table 2 and Discussion section use different terminology for the same regions. Table 2 uses AAL atlas labels (e.g., 'SupraMarginal_R', 'Rolandic_Oper_L') while the Discussion text uses descriptive labels (e.g., 'right superior temporal gyrus', 'left central tegmental sulcus', 'left central sulcus'). The abstract and results text describe 'right superior margin gyrus' and 'left central sulcus' for males, but Table 2 lists 'SupraMarginal_R' and 'Rolandic_Oper_L'. This inconsistency is preserved; both are extracted as reported.

The Discussion section repeatedly refers to 'right superior temporal gyrus' as the common activation in both sexes, but Table 2 and the Results section clearly label the region as 'SupraMarginal_R' (right supramarginal gyrus). These are anatomically distinct regions. The table values are used for coordinate extraction; the Discussion text discrepancy is flagged.

Coordinate space is not explicitly stated in the methods or results. MNI space is inferred from the use of the AAL atlas and SPM12 with DARTEL normalization. All coordinates are labeled as 'not_reported' for coordinate_space_reported_exact with an inference note.
No expectancy, blinding success, or treatment credibility measures were reported or assessed. The paper does not mention sham acupuncture or blinding of participants.
No adverse events section is present in the paper. No statement about adverse events or safety was found.

The paper mentions 'Data analysis is presented in Supplementary material' for the acquisition time section, suggesting additional preprocessing or analysis details may exist in a supplement not provided in this PDF.

The cluster extent units in Tables 2, 3, and 4 are labeled 'Cluster size' and 'Extent' respectively but units (voxels vs. mm³) are not explicitly stated. Extracted as 'voxels (inferred)' based on typical SPM12 reporting convention.

The paper states the activation results use F-values (Table 2) rather than T-values, which is atypical for a two-condition contrast in SPM. This may reflect the use of F-contrasts or F-statistics from the GLM. These are preserved exactly as reported.

The thalamic FC difference results in Table 4 appear to show enhanced FC in females relative to males based on the Results and Discussion text, but the direction of the two-sample t-test (female > male) is inferred from context, not explicitly labeled in Table 4 header. The figure caption for Figure 5 and surrounding text confirm this is the female > male contrast.

The MASS scale is described as including 10 items in the methods ('pain, soreness, pressure, heaviness, fullness, warmth, coolness, numbness, tingling, and dull pain') but Table 1 reports 12 items including 'Aching', 'Deep pressure', 'Heaviness', 'Fullness', 'Warmth', 'Cold', 'Numbness', 'Tingling', 'Dull pain', 'Soreness', 'Sharp pain', and 'Throbbing'. The methods description is less complete than the table. All 12 table items are extracted.

The paper reports both male and female groups enrolled and analyzed differ (enrolled 30M/25F; analyzed 25M/21F). The n values in Table 1 use male n=25 and female n=21, consistent with the analyzed sample. All sensation scores are extracted with the analyzed n values.

The Abstract and Discussion mention 'bilateral thalamus' as seed points, and Table 4 provides separate results for Thalamus_L and Thalamus_R seeds. Based on the Discussion, the Thalamus_L FC results (caudate, precuneus, lingual, postcentral, supplementary motor) reflect females > males, and the Thalamus_R FC results also reflect females > males. However, the Discussion text states 'the right thalamus in males showed enhanced functional connectivity with the left parahippocampal gyrus...' which contradicts Table 4. Table 4 coordinates are used as the authoritative source and extracted as females > males for both seeds.

The paper states bandpass filtering bandwidth as '0.2–0.008 Hz.' This is an unusually wide high-pass cutoff (0.2 Hz) compared to typical rs-fMRI (0.01–0.1 Hz). This may be a typographical error in the paper, but it is extracted exactly as reported.
No sham acupuncture condition was included. The study compares active acupuncture task vs. retained needle baseline (no torsion) within session. There is no placebo or sham arm.
Trial registration number is not reported in the paper.
